sections.heading: C — Knowledge dossier: Stopped vehicles and warning lights
sections.markdown:
## C — Knowledge dossier: Stopped vehicles and warning lights

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A02
South Dakota requires a driver approaching a stopped authorized emergency vehicle using red signals to stop completely before reaching it, regardless of the direction from which the driver approaches. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A02
After the required stop for a stopped emergency vehicle displaying red signals, a motorist may continue cautiously only after checking that it is safe, unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A02
The handbook applies its amber, yellow or blue warning-light rule to motorists approaching any stopped vehicle displaying those lights, from whichever direction they approach. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A02
For a stopped vehicle using amber, yellow or blue lights on a South Dakota interstate or highway with at least 2 lanes traveling in its direction, drivers must move to the farthest lane at least 300 feet in advance, unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A02
After moving to the farthest lane when the multilane amber, yellow or blue warning-light rule applies, a driver must pass the stopped vehicle cautiously unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane highway, the rule for a stopped vehicle showing amber, yellow or blue lights requires a speed at least 20 miles per hour below the posted limit when that limit exceeds 20 miles per hour, unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
When a two-lane highway's posted limit is 20 miles per hour or lower, the amber, yellow or blue stopped-vehicle rule calls for slowing to 5 miles per hour unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane highway, a driver approaching a stopped vehicle displaying amber, yellow or blue warning lights must make the prescribed speed reduction at least 300 feet before reaching it, unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
Under the two-lane-highway rule for a stopped vehicle using amber, yellow or blue warning lights, slowing to the specified speed must be followed by cautious travel unless directed otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A02
The handbook's emergency-vehicle examples include police vehicles, ambulances and fire-department vehicles, while making clear that other emergency vehicles can also be included. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0002]

Misconceptions: A warning light does not always require the same response; match red signals, divided-direction lanes and two-lane roads to their cited rules.
Mnemonics: Use color, road layout, then action as an authored retrieval sequence; the cue adds no rule.
Glossary: Authorized emergency vehicle includes the police, ambulance and fire-service examples in the cited facts; warning-light color identifies the relevant rule.
Dynamic facts: These are edition-bound roadway rules, with no current officeholder or locality value; later legal changes require a source refresh.

ranked.label: Pedagogic emphasis: Choose the response by light color and road layout.

items.why: Red signals and the two warning-light road layouts require distinct response practice.

corpus_stability.reason: The official dated snapshot is pinned, but revision frequency has not been measured. Unknown cadence remains blocked for release pending the section-A verification debt; this is not a claim that the handbook is volatile.
